docs.summary: Fluent builder for a data table. Declare columns with [`Column`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.TableBuilder~Column), add rows with [`Row`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.TableBuilder~Row), then call [`Show`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.TableBuilder~Show). Construct via [`Table`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.Origami~Table).
Override table width (default Stretch).

members.name: Scroll
members.signature: public TableBuilder Scroll(float width, float height)

docs.summary: Fixed pixel size with an internal vertical scroll for the rows (header stays pinned).
Row height in pixels (default 30).

Only build the rows currently scrolled into view (plus a small buffer), padding the rest with spacers so the scrollbar and total height stay exact. Rows are fixed-height, so the visible range is computed directly from the scroll offset. Requires [`Scroll`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.TableBuilder~Scroll); big win for long lists (hundreds+ rows). Row element IDs stay keyed to the data index, so selection, sort and context actions are unaffected.
Draw the outer border + rounded corners (default true). Pass false to embed flush inside a panel.

Draw fully custom content per cell instead of using `.Row().Cell()` data. Set the number of rows with [`RowCount`](#api~Prowl.OrigamiUI.TableBuilder~RowCount); for each row/column the callback is invoked inside the (already laid-out, column-flex-sized, clipped) cell so the host can draw carets, tags, badges, rename fields, etc. while the table owns the column widths, header, selection background and scrolling.
